title: Instantaneous tidal debris return is too short for broad ASASSN-14ko UV flares in the tested precessing giant-star orbit
abstract: We test a necessary flare-duration bound for a proposed precessing giant-star orbit of ASASSN-14ko. We use joint UV flare-fit samples from a signed campaign result. At black-hole mass 10^7.86 solar masses, period 108.44 days and apsidal advance 0.082 radians per orbit, the full ballistic debris return interval is 2.225 days for a one-solar-mass star at tidal penetration factor one and unit tidal energy spread. The fitted cycle-28 UV half-maximum duration is 36.73 days, with a marginal 95 percent range of 28.08-47.91 days. Even a ten-solar-mass star at penetration factor 0.5 gives only 9.60 days. It needs at least 18.48 days of extra launch or response span at the lower width endpoint. A larger debris energy spread can also remove the mismatch. This is a conditional audit of prompt emission from instantaneous ballistic return. It does not reject drag or prove an orbital stall. The inferred tidal dynamical time is 8-10 days, so prolonged stripping must be tested before the extra span is assigned to disc processing.

display.caption: Full debris return intervals in the tested orbit compared with source-fit UV half-maximum durations. The comparison is conditional on simultaneous release, a stated energy spread and prompt emission.
